facts.raw_span: A 31-year-old male nursing student
history of axillary hyperhidrosis
excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum
previously treated his axillary condition successfully with 20% aluminum chloride
treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride was unsuccessful
used absorbent pads yet continued to soak through his pants
consequently unable to attend work
Minor starch-iodine test was performed
Areas of significant sweating were identified in the sacral region (10 × 3-cm area) and intergluteal cleft (6 × 8-cm area)
a 10 × 3-cm grid was drawn on the sacrum and a 6 × 8-cm grid was drawn on the intergluteal cleft
with the outermost dots omitted

concepts.why: The patient's excessive sweating is localized to specific areas, including the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, as identified by the Minor starch-iodine test.
The patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis and unsuccessful treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride suggests a possible compensatory sweating mechanism.
The patient's history of axillary hyperhidrosis and current presentation of excessive sweating in the buttocks area suggest a possible primary hyperhidrosis condition.

rationales.F02: History of axillary hyperhidrosis suggests a possible primary hyperhidrosis condition.
rationales.F03: Excessive sweating of the buttocks, most severe at the intergluteal cleft and sacrum, is a strong indicator of focal hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F04: Previous successful treatment of axillary condition with aluminum chloride may indicate a primary hyperhidrosis condition.
rationales.F05: Unsuccessful treatment of the intergluteal cleft and sacrum with aluminum chloride may suggest compensatory hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F09: Identification of significant sweating areas in the sacral region and intergluteal cleft through the Minor starch-iodine test supports focal hyperhidrosis.
rationales.F10: The grid markings on the sacrum and intergluteal cleft provide further evidence of focal hyperhidrosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's excessive sweating is localized to specific areas (sacral region and intergluteal cleft), which is consistent with Focal Hyperhidrosis, and the Minor starch-iodine test confirmed these areas of significant sweating.
